origins: Retirement, slower pace, and a culture that prizes youth can make older adults feel invisible. Loss of work, driving, or strength adds to the sense of being no longer needed.
teaches: “In old age they will still bear fruit; healthy and green they will remain” (Psalm 92:14). “Gray hair is a crown of glory; it is attained along the path of righteousness” (Proverbs 16:31). “Even to your old age, I will be the same, and I will bear you up when you turn gray.” Anna served God day and night in the temple in her eighties (Luke 2:36–37). Paul told Titus that older men and women are to teach others (Titus 2). Older believers hold wisdom and prayer that the church needs.
self_statements: I have nothing left to give.
Young people do not care what I think.
errors: Believing I am either productive or useless.
Predicting that no one will need me.
Feeling overlooked and concluding that I am useless.
questions: What do I know and have lived through that others could learn from?
Who has asked for my advice or prayers?
What could I give: time, listening, prayer, a skill?
What does Scripture say about the elderly?
Who in my life is lonely and might welcome a call?
What is one way to serve this week?
truth: God still uses me. My years are a crown, and my wisdom and prayers matter. I can bear fruit at every age, in ways large and small.
hw_truths: I still bear fruit in old age.
log: Each week, note one way you encouraged or helped.
actions: Reach out to a person who may be lonely.
Pray by name for family and friends.
Offer to share your experience with someone younger.
prayer: Father, You have promised to carry me in old age. Show me how to serve and bear fruit in this season. Amen.
